get.description:
Keyset-paginated activity feed (trades, splits, merges,
redeems, …) in the standard `{ data, pagination }` envelope.

Ordering is `(block_timestamp, sequence_id)`, `DESC` by default or `ASC` via
`sort_direction=ASC`; both keyset-seekable. Value sorts (`CASH`/`TOKENS`)
have no seek anchor and are rejected with `400` rather than silently
re-served as page one. The cursor binds the direction it was minted under
and the resume ADOPTS it, so a replay cannot flip the walk mid-stream.

A malformed `condition` id is a `400` naming the value; a
well-formed one that matches nothing serves an empty `data` array, which
is the meaningful zero-state; absence means the market is not servable,
and only that.

`condition_id` / `conditionId` are accepted aliases.

direction it was minted under.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description:
Window end, epoch seconds (inclusive); omitted or `0` means now plus
one day.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description:
Gamma event id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values);
resolves to the events' markets. Mutually exclusive with `condition`.

parameters.name: exclude_deposits_withdrawals
parameters.description:
Defaults to `true`, which drops `DEPOSIT` and `WITHDRAWAL` rows from
the page, including when `type` names them. Pass `false` to include
them.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; default 100, max 1000, past-cap rejected.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: BUY or SELL.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Only `TIMESTAMP` is supported (v2 pages by keyset).

parameters.name: sort_direction
parameters.description:
`ASC` or `DESC` (default). The keyset seeks in the chosen direction;
the minted cursor binds it, so pass it consistently when paging.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Window start on `block_timestamp`, epoch seconds (inclusive). Omitted
or `0` floors to three years back; pass `start=1` for full history.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
Activity type(s), comma-separated. Accepted values: `TRADE`, `SPLIT`,
`MERGE`, `REDEEM` (automatic redemptions included), `CONVERSION`,
`MIGRATION`, `REWARD`, `YIELD`, `MAKER_REBATE`, `TAKER_REBATE`,
`REFERRAL_REWARD`, `DEPOSIT`, `WITHDRAWAL`, `DIRECTIONAL_SPLIT`,
`DIRECTIONAL_MERGE`, `THRESHOLD_COMPOSE`, `THRESHOLD_DECOMPOSE`, `TIP`.
Any other value is rejected with `400`. Omitted, the feed returns every
type except `TIP`.

`DEPOSIT` and `WITHDRAWAL` rows are returned only with
`exclude_deposits_withdrawals=false`. Under its default (`true`) they are
dropped even when named here, so `type=DEPOSIT` or `type=WITHDRAWAL`
alone returns an empty page.

`DIRECTIONAL_SPLIT`, `DIRECTIONAL_MERGE`, `THRESHOLD_COMPOSE` and
`THRESHOLD_DECOMPOSE` are operations on range events, whose outcomes are
value buckets and whose lines are ABOVE / BELOW positions over those
buckets. A directional split turns collateral plus the buckets between
two lines into ABOVE the lower line and BELOW the higher one; a
directional merge reverses it. Both are rows of the whole event, so a
`condition` filter never returns them. A threshold compose turns buckets
into one line position and a threshold decompose turns it back; these
rows carry the line's market and side. Split, merge, redeem and
conversion on a range event keep `SPLIT`, `MERGE`, `REDEEM` and
`CONVERSION`.

`TIP` is **opt-in**: it is never in the default set, so it is only
returned when you name it here. A tip is a user↔user pUSD transfer that
is not a trade-settlement leg; `size` is the amount and `side` carries the
direction (`IN` received / `OUT` sent).

get.description:
A keyset page of positions in the standard
`{ data, pagination }` envelope. One route serves a user's open book, their
closed book (`status=CLOSED`), and a market's holders (market anchor).

At least one of `user`/`condition` is required. Supplying both anchors on the
user and applies `condition` as a narrowing filter.

`status` defaults to `OPEN`, which is the **superset**: a
settled-but-unredeemed winner still holds its tokens, so it is an open
position whose condition resolved. `REDEEMABLE` narrows to that subset, and
each row echoes its own `status`.

Resume contract: a `next_cursor` binds the `status`/`sortBy`/`sortDirection`
the walk started with. To follow it, send `cursor` together with the same
`user` or `condition` anchor used on the first page; a bare `?cursor=` request
returns 400. The token is the authority on the spine and the total order,
and the handler adopts all three from it. Restating them is allowed and
must agree;
**explicitly** contradicting one is a 400, because replaying an anchor under
a different spine or order would silently walk a different result set.
Omitting them is not a contradiction; a defaulted `status` is the absence of
a choice, not a request for `OPEN`.
User CLOSED residual sorts bind their realized-PnL ranking in the signed
cursor kind. Earlier cursors for those sorts return 400 and require restarting
pagination without `cursor`, because their numeric anchor has ambiguous units.

A malformed `condition` id is a `400` naming the value; a
well-formed one that matches nothing serves an empty `data` array, which
is the meaningful zero-state; absence means the market is not servable,
and only that.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description:
Condition id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values). With
`user`, narrows that user's positions (all ids honoured). Without
`user`, anchors on the market's holders; exactly one id is accepted
there, and a multi-id list is rejected rather than silently truncated.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque pagination cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`. It
carries the page position, page size, and the status/sort/direction it
was minted under.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description:
Inclusive upper bound on `last_event_at`, epoch seconds; omit or `0` for
unbounded.

A position with no native economics carries no `last_event_at` and is
therefore **excluded by any bound**, in either direction; a window asks
which positions moved inside it, and a row with no clock has no answer.
Unbounded requests still serve those rows.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description:
Event id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values).
User-anchored only.

parameters.name: filter_amount
parameters.description:
The filter floor. `TOKENS`: minimum CURRENT holding in shares
(defaults to the 0.1 dust floor; applies to `OPEN`/`REDEEMABLE`; a
user's `CLOSED` set is not narrowed by it, and on a market anchor it
moves the OPEN/CLOSED boundary). `CASH`: minimum mark-to-market
`current_value` in USDC, on top of the token dust floor. Invalid
values fall back to the default.

parameters.name: filter_type
parameters.description:
`CASH` or `TOKENS`; defaults to `TOKENS` (the /v2/trades-homogenized
filter pair, replacing the former `size_threshold`).

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description:
Also include positions on archived markets; defaults to `false`.
`OPEN`/`REDEEMABLE`/`REDEEMABLE_LOST`/`MERGEABLE` only; combining it with
`status=CLOSED` is rejected. Inactive markets remain excluded either way.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: First-page size. Ignored when `cursor` is supplied (the cursor's size wins).

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
One of `CURRENT_VALUE`, `PRICE`, `TOKENS`, `UNREALIZED_PNL`,
`REALIZED_PNL`, `TOTAL_PNL`, or `TIMESTAMP` (the row's `last_event_at`).
`PRICE` ranks by the response's effective `current_price` on every
supported anchor and status. On `REDEEMABLE`, the existing winners-first
partition remains ahead of the requested price order. The default
follows the status: `CURRENT_VALUE` for `OPEN`/`REDEEMABLE`,
`REALIZED_PNL` for `CLOSED`. On a user's `CLOSED` positions, `TOKENS`,
`CURRENT_VALUE`, `PRICE` and `UNREALIZED_PNL` describe a holding that no
longer exists, so those pages are served in `REALIZED_PNL` order.

parameters.name: sort_direction
parameters.description: `ASC` or `DESC`; defaults to `DESC`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Inclusive lower bound on `last_event_at`, epoch seconds; omit or `0` for
unbounded (the `/v2/activity` + `/v2/trades` vocabulary).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
One of `OPEN`, `REDEEMABLE`, `REDEEMABLE_LOST`, `MERGEABLE`, or `CLOSED`;
defaults to `OPEN`. `REDEEMABLE_LOST` requires `user`, supports all six
sorts, and defaults to `CURRENT_VALUE`; it preserves row status
`REDEEMABLE`. `MERGEABLE` is `OPEN` narrowed to live complementary pairs
(conditions where the wallet holds >= 2 servable-live tokens) and defaults
to `TOKENS`; it is user-scoped, so a market-anchored request renders as
`OPEN`.

`OPEN` is the superset; it includes settled-but-unredeemed winners,
which `REDEEMABLE` narrows to. `CLOSED` is exited positions.

Combo positions for a user, in the standard
`{ data, pagination }` envelope.

Sorts: `FIRST_ENTRY` (default) | `ENTRY_COST` (+ `CURRENT_VALUE` alias) |
`UPDATED`, each with `sort_direction`. `FIRST_ENTRY DESC` pages by the
two-state keyset anchor `(first_entry_at_micros, combo_condition_id,
outcome_index)` (NULL micros = the NULL tail); `UPDATED ASC` by the
single-state `(updated_at_micros, …)` anchor; every other combination by an
offset-shaped token. The cursor binds sort + direction and the resume
ADOPTS them, so a replay cannot flip or re-sort the walk mid-stream.

It binds the cohort; `user`/`status`/`condition`/`updated_after`/
`updated_before`; the same way: following a
page needs nothing but `?user=` (always required here) and `?cursor=`, and
restating a filter is allowed but must agree. Omitting one is not a
contradiction, it is the absence of a choice; **contradicting** one is a
400, because the token's walk state only means anything against the cohort
it was minted on.

Incremental sync: `updated_after`/`updated_before` are an INCLUSIVE
epoch-second window on `updated_at`. Without a `status` filter, either

get.description:
The price-history series for one outcome token, or
a single point-in-time observation.

Three window forms, exactly one per request: `start` (with optional `end`),
`interval`, or `as_of`. Points are served oldest-first; pass `?cursor=` from
a prior response's `next_cursor` for the next page.

`interval=max` (or `all`) serves the market's whole life, back to 2022 for
the oldest markets, at 12-hour buckets unless `bucket_seconds` says
otherwise; explicit `start`/`end` windows cap at 15 days, so the presets
are the long-range path.

The series ends with a **terminal point**: the latest observation inside the
window, which is a real tick and so can fall between bucket boundaries.
Nothing may assume uniform spacing (sparse data already forbids that), and
each point's `resolution_seconds` says what window it was observed in.

**Availability is graded by resolution.** The 3-hour and 12-hour series are
permanent (back to 2022-11-18); the fine grains are windowed, with these
MINIMUMS: 1-minute data at least 7 days, 5-minute at least 60, 30-minute at
least 90. Floors, not exact horizons: data expires in multi-day chunks, so a
grain usually reaches a few days further back than its minimum. Coverage is
measured per request, never assumed from a table, so `bucket_seconds=60`
over a window starting a month ago is an incompatible pair: both values are
valid, and there is no data at their intersection.

The two ways of asking behave differently on purpose:

* **`bucket_seconds` sent** is served exactly as asked, so over a window
  whose resolution has expired you get an empty page rather than a silent
  substitution.
* **`bucket_seconds` omitted** lets the server choose a width that can
  actually serve the window: the finest tier grain whose series stays under
  ~2,500 points, except that a window wider than 12 hours never defaults to
  the 60-second grain (ask for `bucket_seconds=60` explicitly when you want
  it over a longer window), and
  coarsened further if that grain does not reach the window's start. A
  window up to 12 hours keeps 1-minute detail (an hour 60 points, 12 hours
  720); beyond that it moves to a materialized tier (a day 288, three days
  864, a week 2,016, fifteen days 720). Send `bucket_seconds` when you want
  a specific density instead.

A RESOLVED market's series ends with one settlement point: the on-chain
payout of the requested token (0 lost, 1 won, fractional for voided or
split resolutions) at `resolution_seconds` 0, placed one bucket edge past
the last stored row and clamped to an explicit window's `end`. It appears
only on the final page of a paginated walk, and only once the resolution
is settled on-chain; an unresolved market's series is unchanged.

`resolution_seconds` on every point reports what it was served at, so read it
instead of assuming the width a recent window would have given you. For a
multi-day window prefer a grain-aligned `bucket_seconds` (300, 1800, 10800,
43200) or omit it; a 60-second width over days is the one shape that is both
slow and, past 7 days, empty.

parameters.name: bucket_seconds
parameters.description:
Bucket width in SECONDS (60…86400). `bucketSeconds` is an accepted alias.

OMIT it and the server sizes the width to the window: the finest tier
grain (60, 300, 1800, 10800, 43200) that keeps the series under ~2,500
points, except that an explicit window wider than 12 hours never
defaults to the 60s grain (send `bucket_seconds=60` when you want
second-by-minute detail over a longer window), and coarsened further if
that grain no longer reaches the window's start.
So a window up to 12 hours keeps 1-minute detail, half a day through a
week defaults to 300, fifteen days to 1800; interval presets keep their
own span-derived defaults (`1d` 60s, `1w` 300, `1m` 1800, and the
unbounded `max`/`all` 43200).

SEND it and it is served exactly as asked, which for a window older than
that resolution's retention means an empty page rather than a silent
substitution. An explicit value is also floored per interval: 600 for
`max`/`all`/`1m`, 300 for `1w`.

malformed value, not an absent one.

`max`/`all` serve the market's WHOLE life (back to 2022 for the oldest
markets) at 12-hour buckets by default; at `bucket_seconds` of 10800 or
43200 the window is unbounded, while finer widths keep a 30-day window.
The other intervals take a width sized to their own span when
`bucket_seconds` is omitted (`1h`/`6h`/`1d` 60, `1w` 300, `1m` 1800), and
each still floors an explicit value: 600 for `max`/`all`/`1m`, 300 for
`1w`.

growing at the tip, and the 15-day cap is re-checked on every page, so a
walk that starts near the cap can outlive it.

get.description:
How fresh the data behind this API is.

`/readyz` answers whether this pod can reach its datastore; this answers how
far behind chain head what you are reading is. Two halves, because each is
blind exactly where the other sees:

* `serving`; the projections that turn ingested rows into what the feeds
  read (`activity_feed` enrichment, `custody_balances` ingestion, the PnL
  engine).
  Each carries its own clock, so this is the only half that can see
  "everything stopped". `lag_seconds` is the worst age across them and
  `worst` names which one, so a single stalled projection cannot hide behind
  two healthy ones.
* `ingestion`; one crawl cursor per `(contract, event)`, summarised as the
  tail, the furthest-behind block, and the worst few cursors BY NAME. Every
  reading here is relative or positional, so under a total stall it reads
  green; that is why `serving` exists alongside it.

Streams that are dormant by design are dropped from `ingestion` rather than
reported, because they sit arbitrarily far back forever and would otherwise
fill the list and push the stream you care about off it.

Takes no parameters and is not paginated. Served from a snapshot refreshed
in the background, never computed on the request: `computed_at` and
`age_seconds` say how old it is, so a stalled refresher or a datastore
outage shows up as a growing age rather than a 500. Before the first refresh
lands there is nothing to serve and this answers `503`; "not measured yet"
and "measured, no lag" are different claims.

`token_ids`); elements are trimmed, leading zeros stripped and duplicates
collapsed to their first position. `data` holds one row per known id in
request order; an unknown id is simply absent (never a `404`), and an
all-unknown request returns an empty array.

`?condition=`: a comma-separated list of up to 10 condition selectors
(aliases `condition_id`, `conditionId`), each `0x` plus 62 or 64 hex
digits, lower-cased and deduplicated. A ConditionalTokens condition id
returns the market's tokens (for a market carried over to polymarket-v2,
its whole family: the ConditionalTokens pair, then the polymarket-v2
pair); a neg-risk market id returns every market of the structure; a
polymarket-v2 condition id (the value a combo leg carries as
`leg_condition_id`) returns that condition only; the 66-character
condition id of a native polymarket-v2 market returns that market; the
on-chain event id of a polymarket-v2 neg-risk structure returns every
question of it. `data` holds the rows grouped by selector in request
order, then by question index, market, module and outcome slot; an
unknown value contributes nothing.

polymarket-v2 module. Reference fields never change; `closed`,

paginated: `data` is the row array with no `pagination`.

Get the authenticated account's Backstop Liquidity Provider (BLP) enrollment
and the instruments it is subscribed to.

The endpoint is restricted to program participants: an authenticated account
that is not enrolled receives a 404, the same response as an account
requesting a route that does not exist for it. A participant that is enrolled
but not yet subscribed to any instrument receives an empty `instruments`
list.

Program membership is set by Polymarket under the participation agreement.
Subscriptions are the participant's own to manage through
`POST /v1/blp/enroll`; every subscribed instrument runs at the program
leverage of 3x, which is locked while the subscription stands.

post.description:
Subscribe the authenticated Backstop Liquidity Provider (BLP) account to an
instrument, or unsubscribe it. A participant only receives backstop
allocations on the instruments it is subscribed to.

The subscription always applies to the authenticated account — there is no
account parameter. Program membership itself is set by Polymarket under the
participation agreement and cannot be changed here: an authenticated account
that is not enrolled receives a 404, matching
`GET /v1/blp/enrollment`.

**Subscribing sets the instrument's leverage to the program leverage of
3x** before the subscription takes effect, and the instrument's leverage is
then locked for as long as the subscription stands — `PATCH
/v1/trade/leverage` on a subscribed instrument rejects with
`blp_leverage_locked`. The margin mode is left as it is. Unsubscribing
releases the lock and leaves the leverage at 3x; set it to whatever you
want afterwards.

If the leverage change is rejected (for example the instrument's risk tier
caps leverage below 3x), the subscription is not applied and the rejection
is returned unchanged.

The call is idempotent — subscribing an already-subscribed instrument, or
unsubscribing one that was never subscribed, succeeds and changes nothing.
A repeated subscribe leaves the leverage as the first one set it.

get.description:
List the backstop liquidations the authenticated Backstop Liquidity Provider (BLP)
account received, most recent first by default.

Each record is one absorption and carries the same fields as a frame on the
`backstop` WebSocket channel, so a participant that missed frames while
disconnected can replay them from here rather than reconstructing them from
trade history. Records do not identify the liquidated account.

`margin` is the net margin transferred with the positions. It is negative when
the absorption carried bad debt — the fund returned more isolated margin than the
account's balance covered.

Like the other BLP routes, this one is restricted to program participants: an
authenticated account that is not enrolled receives a 404, the same response as an
account requesting a route that does not exist for it.

Get the global perpetuals leaderboard, ranked by PnL, notional volume,
current account value, or ROI across all instruments.

Windows are anchored to calendar UTC boundaries: `day` starts at 00:00 UTC
today, `week` at Monday 00:00 UTC, `month` at the first of the month
00:00 UTC, and `all` at exchange launch.

PnL is realized PnL minus trading fees plus funding payments, consistent
with the account PnL endpoint; unrealized PnL is excluded. Notional is the
USD value of all fills in the window. Every entry carries both metrics;
`rank` is the position under the requested `sort_by`.

ROI sorting uses the served, rounded window ROI in descending order, with
ties broken by higher PnL, higher notional, then the older account. It uses
the same eligible accounts as PnL and notional, with no additional minimum
equity or volume requirement. The optional `address` row reports its rank
under the same ordering, including ranks beyond the pageable top 1000.

PnL, notional, and account value are raw numeric strings from the engine.
Account value is current equity (collateral value plus unrealized PnL).
The background census advances by at most 8,192 accounts on each 60-second
poller tick, so a full publication can span multiple ticks as the account
population grows. For account-value sorting, `timestamp` is the earlier of
the published census start and the historical window's computation time,
so stale membership and PnL remain observable if a historical rebuild fails.
When sorting by account value, the requested window still determines which
accounts and historical PnL/notional metrics are included, while the
ranking uses their current equity. Accounts whose equity cannot be computed
are excluded from that ranking. When unrealized PnL is unavailable (for
example, due to stale marks), the display field falls back to collateral
value on PnL/notional entries and address lookups; it does not establish an
equity rank. `total` counts accounts with published equity in that window.
`sort_by=account_value` returns 503 while the first completed census is
warming. PnL and notional rankings remain available during that warm-up.
Clients are responsible for decimal and currency presentation formatting.

Rankings are recomputed periodically; `timestamp` is the computation time.
Returns 25 entries by default and at most 100 per request; only the top
1000 ranks are pageable (`offset + limit` must not exceed 1000).

Provide `address` to additionally return that account's row regardless of
rank. An address with no activity in the window returns zero metrics and
no rank.

Sends one legacy order heartbeat for the authenticated API key.
The first accepted send enables timeout cancellation for all open orders
owned by that API key, across markets and processes. Keep sending accepted
heartbeats every 5 seconds. No scheduler or disarm operation is provided;
stopping sends or closing a client leaves the deadline active.
It shares the key's registration with POST /v1/heartbeats and resets the
expected modern heartbeat ID to an empty string.
After 10 seconds without an accepted send, a five-second scan removes the
registration and queues a best-effort cancel-all attempt. Cancellation
timing and success are not guaranteed. Later accepted sends register again.
A lost response may follow an accepted send. WebSocket keepalive does not
refresh this deadline. Stop placing orders and explicitly cancel/verify
orders you intend to remove before shutdown.

`include_pnl=true` the per-side GROSS figure, so each side of a hedged

only with `include_pnl=true`.

with `include_pnl=true`.

with `include_pnl=true`.

`include_pnl=true`.

only with `include_pnl=true`.

`entry_cost_usdc`. Served only with `include_pnl=true`.

netted across the market's outcome tokens by default or at per-side gross

`{ data, pagination }` envelope for `/v2/holders`; an offset-cursor
feed (per outcome token): the offset lives behind the opaque token,
never on the wire.

chain_id.description:

is readable in one response.

cursors.description:
How many live streams were found. `0` means no ingestion cursors are
visible to this API at all.

max_synced_block.description:
The tail: the furthest-along cursor. Every `behind_max` is measured
against it, and so is each serving mechanism's `blocks_behind`.

min_synced_block.description:
The furthest-behind LIVE stream's block. Deliberately asymmetric with
`max_synced_block` above, which is over ALL cursors: the tail must not
move with the dormant cut, or excluding a stream would redefine the
distance every other stream is measured against.

oneOf.description:
The single furthest-behind live stream. A stall confined to one stream
while every sibling sits at head is invisible in any aggregate figure.

network.description:
The chain the ingestion cursors were written for, as the datastore
itself names it; NOT as this service is configured. Compared against
`chain_id`, it catches a datastore pointed at the wrong chain, which
otherwise presents as data that is merely wrong. `null` when no stream
declares one.

IngestionFreshness.description:
Ingestion health: one cursor per `(contract, event)` stream.

Every figure here is over the LIVE streams only. Streams that are dormant by
design sit arbitrarily far behind forever; they are dropped outright rather
than reported and flagged, because there is nothing a consumer could do with
them and including them is precisely what makes the list useless.

pnl.description:

equity change net of flows; realized plus mark moves; `all` is the
realized-only lifetime ledger. The two deliberately differ.

rank.description: Rank on the requested board; ties share a rank and the next skips.

user_name.description: Profile display name of the wallet.

volume.description: Both-sides traded volume in shares; never USD.

x_username.description: Linked X handle, when one exists.

`pnl` is realized USDC over the window, base and combo positions unified.
`volume` is both-sides SHARES, not USDC. `rank` is a competition
rank; tied users share one, and the next rank skips.

`{ data, pagination }` envelope for `/v2/leaderboard`; an offset-cursor
board. `rank` ties and skips, so the offset behind the token is the only
sound way to page; never derive a page from a rank.

LeaderboardResponse.description:
Either arm's body. `?user=` answers with one standing; everything else with
a page of the board; genuinely different shapes, so the spec says `oneOf`
rather than pretending one covers both.

pnl.description:
Window PnL in USDC, same semantics as the board rows (finite windows
marked, `all` realized-only).

rank_pnl.description: `None` when unranked on the PnL board.

rank_volume.description: `None` when unranked on the volume board.

user_name.description: Profile display name of the wallet.

volume.description: Both-sides traded volume in shares; never USD.

x_username.description: Linked X handle, when one exists.

The ranked board is materialised per sort, so it can only answer "where does
this user place by PnL" or "by volume", one at a time. This shape comes from
the by-user pivot instead and answers both at once.

A `null` rank means **unranked** for that sort: the user exists in the pivot
but is filtered out of that board.

UserVolume.description:
`/v2/user-volume`: one wallet's trading volume over a whole-day window, in
both units side by side.

`volume` is both-sides SHARES; `volume_usdc` is the same measure in USD;
the bare name is the natural unit and `_usdc` is the denomination, the same

error.description: Error identifier. For domain rejections and transport errors (`401`/`404`/`429`/`500`) this is a stable, machine-readable snake_case identifier that is part of the API contract and safe to branch on, e.g. `insufficient_margin`, `insufficient_balance`, `order_not_found`, `reduce_only_invalid`, `price_outside_bounds`, `position_not_found`, `position_exists`, `open_orders_exist`, `invalid_margin_mode`, `invalid_margin_amount`, `margin_below_required_initial`, `account_liquidating`, `instrument_close_only`, `instrument_settled`, `settlement_price_unavailable`, `settlement_insurance_insufficient`, `settlement_invalid_state`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`. `instrument_close_only` means user orders must reduce an existing position; `instrument_settled` is permanent. name.description: Exchange name used in the EIP-712 domain.

withdrawal_fee.description: Withdrawal transaction fee in decimalized asset units

max_limit_notional.description: Maximum limit order notional value in USD

ui_live_time.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when first-party interfaces may display the instrument. A null value means hidden. This advisory field does not affect trading availability.

open_interest.description: One-sided open interest in number of contracts (total long size, equal to total short size); multiply by mark price for quote-asset notional

volume.description: 24-hour trading volume in quote-asset notional (sum of price times quantity), as a numeric string

exchange_volume.description: Matched trading volume in USD notional for the requested window, as an unformatted numeric string

depth.description: Number of book levels to return

Array of order IDs to cancel. Cancelling an order that has attached

Deadline of the armed auto-cancel schedule, in Unix milliseconds. Zero

How the conditional order sizes itself.

Optional — omit it (do not send `0`) when the parent is created in the same request (inline `CreateOrder.tpsl` or `CreateTpSlArgs.parent`); the gateway auto-wires the child to it. slip_bps.description: Per-order market-trigger slippage cap in basis points. 0 = use the per-instrument default. Clamped to the instrument cap.

TpSlOrderFields.description: TP/SL-specific fields surfaced alongside the regular order shape.

initial_margin.description:
Current collateral backing the position. For cross positions, this is
the required initial margin based on position size, mark price, the
applicable risk tier, and configured leverage. For isolated positions,
this is the position's current equity: signed allocated margin plus

total_maintenance_margin.description: Total maintenance margin across all positions

total_position_value.description: Total notional position value in USD

in_liquidation.description: Whether the account is currently under liquidation

fee_tier.description: Zero-based index into `tiers` of the single perpetual fee schedule returned by `/v1/info/fees`, which applies to every perpetual regardless of category. Builder fees are additional and are not part of this tier. Defaults to 0 without a current tier assignment and is capped at the highest configured tier. WebSocket tier changes appear on the next portfolio update, published every 5 seconds.

account_backstops_cursor.description: Pass the last row id from the previous page as a decimal string. The server resolves its exact timestamp within the authenticated account. An opaque URL-safe unpadded base64 JSON cursor with ts (native nanoseconds) and id is also accepted. Keep the timestamp window unchanged when paging.

Paging follows the `sort` direction (strictly older fills when `sort=desc`, strictly newer when `sort=asc`). taker.description: Whether this side was the taker

fee.description: Signed exchange fee for this trade side, excluding builder_fee. Negative values are rebates

pep.description: Position entry price before the fill

liq.description: Whether this fill was part of a liquidation of the account's position — true on forced closes and on any fill executed while the account was under liquidation on the instrument, maker or taker. False on the counterparty leg of an auto-deleveraging or backstop match — its fill is part of someone else's liquidation, flagged by `adl` where applicable

data.description:
- `1767225600000` - Timestamp

sz.description: Signed position size in no. of contracts (positive = long, negative = short)

counterparty.description: Counterparty account address in hex format

volume_7d.description: Rolling 7-day perpetual trading volume in USD

taker_volume_7d.description: Rolling 7-day perpetual taker volume in USD

maker_volume_7d.description: Rolling 7-day perpetual maker volume in USD

account_maker_share_7d.description: Rolling 7-day account maker volume divided by total exchange volume

entity_maker_share_7d.description: Rolling 7-day entity maker volume divided by total exchange volume

actions_per_minute.description: Order action tokens used by the account in the current minute

maker_share_7d.description: Rolling 7-day account maker volume divided by total exchange volume

reward_pool.description: Configured reward pool for the instrument

account_oi.description: Daily average gross open-interest notional for this account across all instruments

Number of times auto-cancel has fired for this account during the

Unix-ms timestamp of the next UTC midnight when the daily trigger
count resets to zero.

referrals_available.description: Remaining lifetime referrals for this invite code.

read_at.description: When the recipient marked this notification read, Unix milliseconds; null if unread.

blp.description: True when the account is enrolled in the Backstop Liquidity Provider program.

Instruments the account is subscribed to, in ascending instrument-id
order. Empty when the account is enrolled but not yet subscribed to
any instrument.

blp_cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Pass the liquidation ID of the last record from the previous page to fetch the next page. Paging follows the `sort` direction (strictly older records when `sort=desc`, strictly newer when `sort=asc`).

blp_sort.description: Time sort direction. `desc` (default) returns the most recent liquidations first; `asc` returns the oldest first.

BlpLiquidationTrade.description: One trade booked for a position absorbed in the liquidation.

trades.description: Trades booked for the positions absorbed in this liquidation, in the order they were booked.

BlpLiquidation.description: One absorption of an account's positions and margin, matching a single `backstop` WebSocket frame.

A collateral-only display fallback does not establish an equity rank.

builder_fee.description: Actual additional builder fee in the same asset as fee, floored independently for each execution to that asset's token decimals (six for pUSD), with discarded dust and no carry. The fee is non-negative and is zero for older or untagged fills and excluded forced liquidation legs.

builder_fee_rate.description: Additional builder fee as a decimal fraction of executed notional, from 0 through 0.001 (10 basis points). Zero approval revokes future admission. Never a percentage string.

earning_id.description: Stable side-specific receipt identity, unique for this builder. Use this to deduplicate, not sequence or trade_id alone.

trader.description: Main address of the attributed trading account, not its signing proxy or the counterparty.

client_order_id.description: Included only when the attributed order supplied a client_order_id.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation preserving account, time window and fully indexed cutoff. Reuse unchanged.

as_of_sequence.description: Complete indexed event prefix shared with the summary. Never the largest row seen.

notional.description: Eligible executed notional including zero-fee fills.

trader_count.description: Distinct trading accounts with at least one attributed fill in this window and indexed cutoff, including zero-fee fills and counting once across markets, assets and maker/taker roles.

active_approval_count.description: Current positive, unrevoked approvals to this builder. This count is independent of the historical window and cutoff. Disabling a builder or platform admission does not erase grants.

enabled.description: Builder is enabled for new requests. Existing saved terms remain valid when disabled.

admission_enabled.description: Platform builder code admission switch. Initially false.

builder_approval_version.description: Exactly the previous version plus one, starting at 1. Revocation retains the version and prevents signed approval replay.

total_fee.description: Exact signed sum of exchange fee and builder_fee in the same asset. May be negative when exchange rebates exceed the builder charge.

Builder.description: Saved builder terms. Address is the registered Perps account, and fee_rate is an additional fraction of executed notional. Terms survive approval revocation for existing orders.

display_symbol.description: Optional presentation override for the full instrument symbol, such as USA500-USD. Use display_symbol when present and fall back to symbol otherwise. This is a label, not an identifier; use instrument_id for trading and storage. Canonical symbol, base_asset, and price-feed identifiers are unchanged. Metadata normally refreshes once per minute; HTTP caching can add delay.

registered.description: Whether the address has a Perps account.

roi.description: Return on investment over the window as a fraction, not a percentage ("0.4527" is 45.27%): `pnl / max(100, starting_equity + max_net_deposits)`. `pnl` is this row's `pnl`. `starting_equity` is the account equity sampled last before the window start (0 for `all`, and 0 for accounts with no earlier sample). `max_net_deposits` is the running maximum, over the window, of cumulative credited deposits minus withdrawals plus transfers in minus transfers out, starting from 0 at the window start; it is never negative. The 100 USD floor keeps tiny accounts from producing extreme ratios. Rounded half-even to 6 decimal places with trailing zeros removed; "0" when `pnl` is 0.

qualified.description: Reached the minimum volume and is ranked

funding.description: Funding received net of funding paid

volume_to_qualify.description: Unboosted volume still needed to rank; "0" once qualified

qualification_progress.description: Fraction of the minimum reached, from "0" to "1"

spots_from_prize_zone.description: Places between this rank and the last paid place; 0 inside the prize zone; absent when unranked

score_to_prize_zone.description: Score still needed to reach the prize zone; "0" inside it; absent when unranked

locked_positions.description: Positions open at the start, by market, including ones since released.

all_markets.description: Every perpetual counts, including markets listed during the competition. When false only `markets` count.

markets.description: When `all_markets` is true, only the boosted markets; otherwise every counted market with its boost.

min_volume.description: Unboosted notional volume needed to rank, as a numeric string

count_unrealized.description: Whether unrealized PnL on open qualifying positions counts

paid_places.description: Size of the prize zone (ranks 1 to paid_places)

participants.description: Accounts with at least one counted fill

final_results.description: The leaderboard shows frozen end-of-competition results

pnl.description: Competition PnL after fees, funding and liquidation losses

qualified.description: Whether the account meets the entry gate. Present only with `include_unqualified=true`.

prize.description: Projected prize while live, prize won once ended; absent outside the prize zone

paid_at.description: Payment time in Unix milliseconds once paid

size_at_start.description: Signed position size at the start (positive long, negative short)

released_at.description: When it was fully closed and the market started counting, in Unix milliseconds; absent while still locked

CompetitionLockedPosition.description: A position open when the competition started. Its market does not count until it is fully closed.

boost.description: Volume multiplier as a numeric string; "1" when not boosted

CompetitionMarket.description: A market in the competition. `boost` multiplies its volume toward boosted volume (never PnL).

amount.description: Prize per trader in the prize asset, as a numeric string

CompetitionPrizeTier.description: One band of the prize table. Every rank from `from_rank` to `to_rank` inclusive is paid `amount`.

sector_label.description: Theme or sector label, e.g. "Semis"; empty when none

prize_pool.description: Total prize pool as a numeric string

internal.description: Visible only to its allowlist (internal test competitions)

CompetitionWidget.description: The live competition at a glance for the trading page. Without a live competition only `timestamp` is present.

arts.description: Gateway arrival timestamp captured at handler entry, in Unix milliseconds.

competition_include_unqualified.description: List the traders still short of the entry gate after the ranked board. Ignored for a lottery or raffle board.

competition_row_state.description: How a leaderboard row is shown. `live` while running (prize is projected), `provisional` while in review, `disqualified` for a rule violation, `final` once results are finalized, `paid` once the prize is paid.

competition_score.description: Competition score, PnL × √(boosted volume), as a numeric string rounded to 6 decimal places. Can be negative.

competition_status.description: Competition lifecycle status. `upcoming` before start, `live` while running, `in_review` from the end until every prize is paid (ranks can still change after disqualifications), `ended` once results are final and every prize is paid.

CompetitionRead_error.description: Error identifier. For domain rejections and transport errors (`401`/`404`/`429`/`500`) this is a stable, machine-readable snake_case identifier that is part of the API contract and safe to branch on, e.g. `insufficient_margin`, `insufficient_balance`, `order_not_found`, `reduce_only_invalid`, `price_outside_bounds`, `position_not_found`, `position_exists`, `open_orders_exist`, `invalid_margin_mode`, `invalid_margin_amount`, `margin_below_required_initial`, `account_liquidating`, `instrument_close_only`, `instrument_settled`, `settlement_price_unavailable`, `settlement_insurance_insufficient`, `settlement_invalid_state`, `settlement_close_only_required`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`. `instrument_close_only` means user orders must reduce an existing position; `instrument_settled` is permanent. Settlement readiness errors leave the instrument and accounts unchanged. For `400` it is a human-readable validation detail whose wording may change. See the Error handling guide for the domain identifiers. (Post-only / Fill-or-Kill outcomes are order statuses such as `post_only_rejected`, not rejections.)

ref.description: Unique server-generated rejection reference. Include this value when asking support to locate the corresponding structured rejection trace.

CompetitionRead_timestamp.description: decision time in Unix milliseconds: terminal event time for event-backed outcomes, gateway decision time otherwise

close_only.description: Whether user orders must be reduce-only. Pricing, funding, and risk management continue until settlement.

settlement_sequence.description: Engine sequence of the accepted instrument settlement event.

settlement_timestamp.description: Settlement cutoff as integer Unix milliseconds. The trailing 30-minute index average ends at this time.

settlement_price.description: Final settlement price from the trailing 30-minute time-weighted index average. Every remaining position closes at this price with no settlement fee.

settlement_insurance_debit.description: Total quote asset amount debited from the insurance fund to cover eligible settlement deficits.

InstrumentSettlement.description: Permanent settlement record. Its sequence and timestamp are the cutoff after which all unapplied funding is waived. Previously applied funding is preserved. An instrument with this record is delisted and cannot resume trading.

settlement_fill.description: Whether this fill closes a position during permanent instrument settlement. Settlement fills use the final settlement price and have no fees or liquidation penalties; they are not normal market trades or ADL.

history_fills.description: Selected public AccountTrade fill keys, in response order. Deduplicated by (instrument_id, trade_id).

trade_id.description: Decimal UInt64 trade ID from the public fills API.

timestamp.description: Public fill timestamp in Unix milliseconds.

history_as_of_at.description: Event time of the serving gateway's captured state and completed-history prefix, in Unix milliseconds. Missing trades are not_found at this horizon; horizons can differ by gateway.

position_cycle_id.description: Opaque stable cycle identity; a flip creates a new identity.

started_at.description: Cycle opening timestamp in Unix milliseconds.

as_of_at.description: Captured state time for active positions; selected fill time for history. Unix milliseconds.

size_after.description: Absolute remaining quantity; side provides its direction.

entry_price.description: Remaining position's weighted entry; last entry before closing when flat. Formatted to instrument price precision.

as_of_price.description: Captured mark for active positions; selected fill price for historical snapshots.

pnl.description: Gross unrealized PnL on remaining size while open; gross realized cycle PnL when closed. Excludes fees, funding and previous cycles.

pnl_percent.description: PnL times leverage divided by entry notional, times 100. Open cycles use unrealized PnL and entry notional on remaining size, excluding realized partial closes. Closed cycles use total opening/add notional, including re-additions after partial closes. Only returned to the authenticated owner; otherwise null. Uses nominal entry margin; portfolio return_on_equity uses actual initial margin and may differ.

leverage.description: Only returned to the authenticated account owner; otherwise null. Current leverage for active positions; captured selected-fill leverage for history, never today's setting. Uncaptured values are null, including fills from older, mixed-version or rollback writers. Replaying a fill without leverage capture can turn a previously captured value to null.

position.description: Normalized horizontal chart coordinate from 0 to 1.

competition_first_fill_at.description: Time of the account's first counted fill in this competition, in Unix milliseconds; absent when unavailable or the account has no counted fills. Ranked ties use the configured tie-breaks, normally boosted volume then first fill order. Fill order can distinguish fills within the same millisecond.

maker.description: Ethereum address of the maker (In the default case, this is your proxy address)

tokenId.description: Token ID (asset ID) for the order

makerAmount.description: Amount the maker is providing in fixed-math with 6 decimals

takerAmount.description: Amount the taker is providing in fixed-math with 6 decimals

expiration.description: Unix timestamp when the order expires. Present in the API wire body; not part of the CLOB V2 EIP-712 signed order struct.

Error429Response.description:
Too Many Requests. `error` distinguishes the limit that was hit:
`ip_rate_limited` (per-IP token bucket), `action_rate_limited` (per-account
action rate), or `open_orders_limit` (resting open-order cap).

Retry-After.description:
Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Present only on token-bucket
rate-limit rejections (`ip_rate_limited` and `action_rate_limited`); a
conservative estimate of when enough capacity will have refilled to
admit the request. Absent on `open_orders_limit`, which is a capacity
limit, not a rate limit — waiting does not free order slots; cancel
resting orders or wait for fills instead.

Error503Response.description:
Service unavailable — safe to retry with backoff, honoring
`Retry-After` when present. `error` is
`service_unavailable`.

Most causes are a request deliberately shed before it reached the
engine, so the request definitely did not execute: the replica's
pod-level in-flight cap (shed before dispatch, with `Retry-After`), a
database read shed as backpressure under overload (by the local read
gate or by the database server's concurrency cap — the query never
executed), a required internal cache that is stale or not yet primed
and would return wrong data, or a full bounded deferred-write queue.

On a subset of order/state-mutating routes, this status is also
returned when the engine round-trip itself times out with zero
responses observed. That is retryable engine backpressure, but —
unlike the sheds above — it does not prove non-execution: the command
may already have been admitted, with its response simply not reaching
the gateway before the deadline. This status is only used for that
case on routes that are safe to retry regardless (idempotent
state-setting, or an engine-side replay guard); routes where a bare
retry cannot safely resolve the ambiguity keep the outcome a
non-retryable 500 instead.

Retry-After.description:
Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Present on pre-dispatch
in-flight-cap sheds — a transient overload signal, so the hint is
short and constant.

failures are returned as a single rejected item so batch endpoints
always return an array. The `error` field is a human-readable validation
detail.

tags.description:
Relayer API keys let a user authenticate requests to relayer endpoints without Gamma auth.
However, Relayer API keys can only be created using Gamma auth. Every address can create a maximum of 100 keys.

The API key auth headers are:
- `RELAYER_API_KEY`
- `RELAYER_API_KEY_ADDRESS`

`RELAYER_API_KEY_ADDRESS` must match the address that owns the key.
